newsitem.title: USA: Fortress to buy Don Galloway for $21 mln.
newsitem.headline: Fortress to buy Don Galloway for $21 mln.

text.p: Fortress Group Inc said Tuesday it agreed to buy Don Galloway Homes Inc of Charlotte, N.C., for $21 million.
The home manufacturer said the acquisition, which it expects to close August 31, will add $0.06 a share to Fortress' earnings for the remainder of 1997.
On a pro-forma basis, Fortress projected Galloway to add $0.20 a share for the whole of 1997, assuming it had bought Galloway on January 1.
An August 15 First Call consensus estimate of two analysts had put the company's earnings at $0.35 a share for the third quarter, $0.48 a share in the fourth quarter, and $1.14 for the full year.

Fortress said it will pay for Don Galloway $5 million in cash; $5 million in a short-term note; $6 million in newly-issued zero dividend convertible and redeemable preferred stock; and an earnout of up to $5 million, which it will pay through the year 2000.

Fortress said Don Galloway posted a pre-tax profit of $7.8 million on gross revenues of $66 million (delivering 470 homes) for the fiscal year ended June 30. Don Galloway's backlog stood at 235 homes with a total value of $33 million as of June 30, Fortress added.
Fortress added it used the proceeds of a recent Lazard Freres Real Estate Investors LLC affiliate's investment in the company to finance the acquisition.
The home manufacturer announced August 15 Lazard affiliate Prometheus Homebuilders LLC agreed to invest $75 million in Fortress and considered investing up to $25 million more in 1999.
Fortress' stock rose 1/16 to 5-1/4 Tuesday morning.
